tools.name: find-threads
tools.title: Find Threads
tools.description: Find the user's Delta threads (conversations with coding agents) by topic or creation date, or list the most recent ones. Returns IDs, titles, short summaries, keywords and links.

tools.name: read-thread
tools.title: Read Thread
tools.description: Read one Delta thread by ID: its summary, goals and a compact transcript of what the user and the coding agent said.

tools.title: Create Draft Thread
tools.description: Create a Delta thread with a draft prompt and open it in Delta for the user to review and send. Asks for confirmation.

tools.name: archive-thread
tools.title: Archive Thread
tools.description: Archive or unarchive one Delta thread by ID. Nothing is deleted. Asks for confirmation.

ai.instructions:
Delta threads are conversations between the user and coding agents in the Delta app; each has an ID, a title, a short generated summary and a transcript. The user writes in English and Russian, and so are the threads.

Answering questions about past work: call find-threads with 1 to 4 distinctive topic words (project, feature, error or file names), not the whole question. A thread matches when it mentions any of the words as written, so if nothing is found, try once more with a synonym, the other language or a shorter form of the word, and with includeArchived. For questions about a period (today, this week), call find-threads without a query and with createdAfter. Then call read-thread on the most relevant threads, at most 3, before answering anything about decisions, details, status or next steps; summaries alone are only enough for overviews and lists. If a thread can't be read, answer from its summary and say so. Never invent thread contents; if nothing relevant is found, say that.

Answer in the language the user writes in. Mention each thread you used as a Markdown link with its title as the text and its link field as the URL.

Only call create-draft-thread or archive-thread when the user explicitly asks to create, archive or unarchive a thread. Thread IDs always come from find-threads; never guess one. To archive several threads, call archive-thread once per thread.

evals.input: @delta What did we decide about the PantryPal push to GitLab?

threads.title: PantryPal
threads.summary: Pushed PantryPal to GitLab; the first push failed with 'shallow update not allowed'.

read-thread.title: PantryPal
read-thread.summary: Pushed PantryPal to GitLab; the first push failed with 'shallow update not allowed'.
read-thread.transcript:
USER
Push to GitLab fails with 'shallow update not allowed'.

AGENT
The clone is shallow. We decided to keep the old remote history in a backup branch, unshallow the repository and then force push main.

expected.meetsCriteria: Says the decision was to back up the old history in a branch, unshallow the repository and force push main, and links the PantryPal thread as a Markdown link

scripts.prepublishOnly:

It seems like you are trying to publish the Raycast extension to npm.

If you did intend to publish it to npm, remove the \`prepublishOnly\` script and rerun \`npm publish\` again.
If you wanted to publish it to the Raycast Store instead, use \`npm run publish\` instead.

" && exit 1
